newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Santer scorns Major's attack on EU employment laws.
newsitem.headline: Santer scorns Major's attack on EU employment laws.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer launched a robust defence of European Union employment laws on Wednesday, dismissing British Prime Minister John Major's claim that they curb Europe's competitiveness.
"Good industrial relations strengthen (competitiveness), they do not weaken it," Santer said in a statement issued to counter Major's charges.

In a hard-hitting speech to about 400 business leaders in Brussels on Tuesday, Major extolled his country's faith in enterprise and the individual, disparaging the "European Social Model" which he said stifled job creation.
"Over-regulation doesn't work, and as a result nor do millions of Europeans," he said, adding that signing the Social Chapter would cost half a million British jobs.

Britain has an opt-out from the EU's Social Chapter, a package of employment laws. The likelihood that Britain's Labour Party would sign the Social Chapter if it wins the pending election is expected to be a major campaign issue.
Santer said it was wrong to say that the Social Chapter and competitiveness were incompatible.
"Not only are they compatible, they are complementary," he said. "Let us stop the caricatures.
